title: pools.ts accepts arbitrary sortBy/sortDirection without validation, passing unverified input into PoolService queries
reasoning: sortBy and sortDirection are read from query params and blindly cast to SortField/SortDirection even though the documented contract (header comment lines 29-30) is only tvl|volume|fees|created and asc|desc. Any other value (e.g., sortBy=1;DROP or sortDirection=random) flows into PoolQueryOptions and down to the SQL layer: invalid values produce 500 responses with raw error strings instead of 400s, and if PoolService interpolates the column/direction into ORDER BY rather than mapping a whitelist, this is a SQL injection vector (service internals are not in the included files, so the concrete confirmed impact is the unvalidated pass-through and 500-vs-400 behavior).
recommendation: Validate sortBy against the whitelist and sortDirection against asc|desc at the route boundary, returning 400 for unknown values; keep any ORDER BY column mapping as a constant whitelist in the service.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No pools route tests are included; the only test file covers price-guard's pure function.
suggestedRegressionTest: Test that GET /pools?sortBy=invalid and ?sortDirection=invalid return 400, and that each of the four valid sortBy values with both directions returns 200.
